status: An owner-ruled addition to the surface contract, recorded beside the Product Designer's authored artifact rather than edited into it. It declares where focus lands after each transition C-10 names, so a test can read the destination instead of restating it.
why: A test that names its own expected focus target proves the code agrees with the test. Reading the destination from the specification proves the code agrees with the specification, which is what C-10 asks and what the Release Reviewer said was missing.
addressing: Each target names the value of the data-focus-target attribute on the element that must hold focus. The attribute exists so that focus is addressable as a contract term rather than by a selector a test invents.

transitions.when: a deferral is submitted with no reason
transitions.why: the field the person must correct, so correcting it requires no navigation

transitions.when: a deferral is submitted with a reason past its bound
transitions.why: the text is preserved and the caret returns to it

transitions.when: a deferral is submitted with an absent, malformed or past review date
transitions.why: the field the person must correct
the only action still available, and the one a person who acted by mistake reaches for
same destination as acknowledgement; the decision was recorded and is reversible
there is no longer an undo control to hold focus, and the status is what changed

transitions.when: the storage adapter rejects a save
transitions.why: the input is preserved and retry is the next action

transitions.when: a save begins and the action controls become disabled
transitions.why: disabling the focused control would otherwise drop focus to the document body, which C-10 forbids

transitions.when: the component mounts and the storage adapter returns a previously saved state
transitions.why: a person returning to a decision that already carries history is told what it is now, rather than left on the document body
